head: pr17421-r17
report:
I found three defects to fix before merge. All three come from the new Python bridge fallback, `sessionRegistrations`, in `src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts`. I ran one probe, `pybridge.test.ts` in the scratch dir, against the real `ensurePyToolBridge` / `registerPyToolBridge` / HTTP server. Ten related existing test files passed (396/0): `test/internal-urls`, the `test/task` and `test/tools/read-artifact*` artifact tests, `persisted-agent-artifacts`, `eval/artifact-readiness`, `eval/worker-core` and `artifacts-concurrency`. None of them covers the cases below.

I only had time to review the eval and artifact-read half of the patch closely. The resume-as-fork, artifact-copy and claim code in `session-manager.ts` (about 2,500 lines of diff) was not reviewed beyond `captureState`, `commitSessionSwitch` and `restoreState` and their callers. I found no leak of the snapshot holder there: the switch's `try` exits only through commit or rollback, and the other callers commit in `finally`.

## 1. Any tool call carrying a dead or invented run id now runs under the newest cell's entry

**Mechanism.** `startServer` now looks up the entry with `registrations.get(\`${session}:${run}\`) ?? sessionRegistrations.get(session)`.
- Before this change the fallback was `registrations.get(sessionId)`. Every key is `session:run`, so that lookup never matched, and a request from a run that had ended got `No active Python tool bridge session`.
- Now every cell writes its entry into `sessionRegistrations`, and that entry is never removed when the cell ends.
- The new gate only checks that `run` is non-empty unless `name === "__artifacts_ready__"`. Any non-empty run id therefore passes for every tool and is served with the most recent cell's `toolSession`, `signal`, `emitStatus` and `shadowCell`.

This undoes the "a cell owns its bridge calls" rule the comment claims to keep ("Everything else still has to say which cell it is"). An `asyncio` task started in a cell keeps `_CURRENT_RID` through contextvars. Once that cell has finished, the task can still run `tool.bash`, `agent()` or a write. That work is then charged to a different cell's display and abort, or to no live cell at all.

**Trigger.** Register an entry with `registerPyToolBridge("sess-A","run-1",…)` and call the returned unregister function (the cell has ended). Then POST `/v1/tool` with `{session:"sess-A", run:"run-1", name:"definitely_not_a_tool"}`.

**Measured.**
```
stale-run: {"ok":false,"error":"Unknown tool from js runtime: definitely_not_a_tool"}
bogus-run: {"ok":false,"error":"Unknown tool from js runtime: definitely_not_a_tool"}   // run:"never-existed"
```
Both requests reached `callSessionTool` and were dispatched. The base commit answers `No active Python tool bridge session: sess-A:run-1`.

**Fix.** Use the session-level fallback only when `runId === ""` and `name === EVAL_ARTIFACTS_READY_BRIDGE_NAME`.

## 2. Background artifact reads fail after the last cell was cancelled or its turn was aborted

**Mechanism.**
- The cell-less `__artifacts_ready__` request is served by the last cell's entry and goes through `callSessionToolPromptOnAbort`.
- That function rejects when `entry.abortRequested()` is true. The value comes from `abortShield.abortRequested`, which stays `true` after `dispose()`.
- It also passes `entry.signal` (the turn signal of the last cell) into `resolveSettledArtifact`, which throws if that signal is aborted.

Before this change, `_artifact_file` in `prelude.py` listed the directory itself, so these reads worked. Now `_artifact_file` always goes through the bridge, and the patch's own target case breaks: a thread left behind by a cell that was cancelled or timed out, which is the usual way such threads outlive their cell. Its `read("artifact://N")` raises until another Python cell runs.

**Trigger.** Register with `abortRequested: () => true`, or with a `signal` that is aborted later, then unregister. Then POST `{session, run:"", name:"__artifacts_ready__", args:{id:"3", root:<dir holding 3.bash.log>}}`.

**Measured.**
```
after-cancel:     {"ok":false,"error":"bridge call \"__artifacts_ready__\" aborted: eval cell was interrupted"}
after-turn-abort: {"ok":false,"error":"bridge call \"__artifacts_ready__\" aborted: eval cell was interrupted"}
```
The artifact file exists in both cases.

**Fix.** Answer the cell-less readiness call without the stale cell's abort state. Call `resolveSettledArtifact(entry.toolSession, …)` directly, with no turn signal or with a session-lifetime one.

## 3. `sessionRegistrations` leaks entries, and one kernel's shutdown removes another's entry

**Mechanism.** Entries are removed only by `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession`, which only `shutdownInvalidatedSession` calls.
- **Per-call mode.** `executePerCall` gives every call a new `bridgeSessionId = py-bridge:<uuid>`, and `executeWithKernelBase` registers it. Nothing ever removes it. Each per-call `eval` therefore leaves one entry for the life of the process, holding a `ToolSession` (and through it the agent session) plus that call's signals. Finding #1 makes the leaked entries usable: any request naming that session id is still served.
- **Dispose.** `disposePyToolBridge` clears `registrations` but not `sessionRegistrations`.
- **Shared key.** The map is keyed by `bridgeSessionId` (the session id). The kernel registry key is `sessionId\0cwd\0interpreter`. Two kernels for one session (different cwd or interpreter) share one entry, so resetting or shutting down one deletes the entry the other kernel's background threads use. Those threads then get `No active Python tool bridge session` until that kernel runs another cell.

**Trigger.** Run Python `eval` in per-call kernel mode N times; `sessionRegistrations.size` grows by N. This is inferred from the code: the map is not exported, so I did not measure it directly. The probe's "served after unregister" result in #1 shows the same persistence.

**Fix.** Remove the session entry in `executePerCall`'s `finally` and in `disposePyToolBridge`. Key the standing entry by kernel, or count references per session, rather than one slot per session id.
